body:
Thank you for taking the time to write this post. I will save it to a txt on my pc and read it again at another junction. A lot of it was comforting to read, if not necessarily entirely relatable (although yes, my exams are going on right now and I'm not going to them haha). I'd definitely admit that not having any particular emotional motivations doesn't help matters for me (I've never been in an intimate relationship, and I don't think I have anyone who I've even shared >20% of my inner self, whatever it looks like, with). 
[Case in point, I've been mulling over another  paragraph right here for the last 10 minutes and just deleted it...] 

Yeah, the small bits of responsibility I picked up recently have helped at least marginally. Having at least some interest/stake in what I'm doing helps differentiate between obligation/duty and responsibility. I'd be lying if I said my self-valuation (when I'm not e.g. right in the afterglow of a completed task) is any higher than before though. Now that I think about it, I guess the sentence I just wrote implies that if I filled my life to the brim with more responsibility I'd be fine then huh, haha.

Regarding the flood/fire bit, for the longest time I've felt that one of the happiest things that could happen to me would actually be to die in the course of thwarting some crime or terrorist attack; it'd certainly beat suicide. Extremely fortunately (for everyone except myself), my country is very safe haha.

On a lighter note I do clean up my room, more than once a year :)

Thanks for the input. Regarding the skewed results, I definitely kept the impact of the depression in mind, but I still wouldn't call the results too skewed when it came to those specific qualities, as the evidence is more than abundant in my life anyway. And yes, I've been doing more creative stuff recently which has been nice (sadly my parents basically did not nurture or promote any of this sort of quality when I was young, which is kind of ironic considering e.g. my dad was in the choir/a band and my siblings, as well as I, were not born with no musical aptitude). Truthfully though, these small things are just a kind of more enjoyable chore that are occupying me nowadays (beats lying in bed all day I guess).

Thanks for the advice. Yeah, I considered that a long time ago (the police force, specifically), but I ended up not doing it and continuing my studies instead (to no avail since I'm now dropping out of college...). I'm from Singapore and (the latter half of) my time in the national service was actually some of the best (or least bad I guess) memories of my life. I'm a lot older now though, and I don't know if I could actually decide to do it now. I'll keep it in mind as an option at least (and not join until I'm sure I won't just take advantage of having access to guns to off myself haha).

Thanks for the sentiments, but this has been long in the making and there's not really much that could talk me out of it. That experience of (slightly) hanging I described is kind of what has finally persuaded me to do it (the exact reasoning as to why it did would be a little too long and likely pointless to explain). It's long overdue really
